subject: Information Theory
title: Chemical Signaling
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Chemical Signaling.

hook.text: A single hormone molecule can trigger a cascade affecting millions of enzymes. One bit of signal, massive amplification.

buildup.text: Cells communicate using chemical signals: hormones, neurotransmitters, and cytokines sent through the body.

discovery.text: Each signaling pathway is a noisy channel. Ligand binding is probabilistic, and downstream responses vary.

twist.text: Cells use redundant pathways. Multiple signals converge on the same response, ensuring reliability.

climax.text: Chemical signaling channels have measurable mutual information between input concentration and output response.

punchline.text: One molecule starts a cascade. Chemistry carries the signal.

quiz.question: Why do cells use redundant signaling pathways?
options: To ensure reliable communication despite noisy channels
